ai.title: Return messageId from stream generators instead of Promise resolve
ai.summary: The `promptAiSdkStream` generator now returns `messageId` directly upon completion, replacing the side-effectful `resolveMessageId` callback and `messageIdPromise` pattern. Callers in `run-agent-step.ts` and `processStreamWithTools` consume this return value via manual `stream.next()` loops to capture the ID without race conditions. Type signatures for `addAgentStep` and related state objects updated to accept `string | null` for `messageId`. This refactoring simplifies async coordination in `backend/src/agent-run.ts` and `backend/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes generating a reply, the system used to hand the reply's unique ID to you through a side channel, a kind of callback that could arrive at an unpredictable moment, sometimes before you were ready or after you'd already moved on. Now the ID is returned directly as the result of the generation step, so you get it at the exact moment the reply finishes, with no waiting or racing. If you watch the backend logs you'd see the ID arriving in sequence with the final chunk of text rather than popping up separately afterward; tests and the agent-running code were updated to accept a value that may be null when no ID is produced. The change is live today and affects every streamed assistant turn, making the ID reliably available to the parts of the system that tag and track

ai.title: SDK bundles ripgrep binaries, drops @vscode/ripgrep
ai.summary: The SDK now vendors ripgrep 14.1.1 binaries for x64/arm64 on Windows/macOS/Linux, replacing the `@vscode/ripgrep` dependency. A new `scripts/fetch-ripgrep.ts` downloads and extracts these binaries into `sdk/vendor/ripgrep/`, which `scripts/build.ts` copies to `dist/vendor/ripgrep/` during build. The `sdk/src/native/ripgrep.ts` module resolves the binary path at runtime via `getBundledRgPath()`, supporting ESM/CJS contexts and an optional `CODEBUFF_RG_PATH` override. `sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts` uses this new resolver, and `sdk/src/index.ts` exports `ToolHelpers` and the native ripgrep utilities.

eli5.text: The SDK now ships with its own copy of ripgrep, a fast file-searching tool, bundled directly into the package for Windows, macOS, and Linux on both Intel and Apple Silicon processors. Previously, it relied on an external copy from a separate project, which meant it could break if that external project changed or became unavailable. If you inspect the package, you will now see ready-to-run search tool binaries sitting inside it, and the package will automatically pick the right one for your computer instead of going looking elsewhere for it.

That single file loads faster in your coding editor, and some duplicate parts that could confuse tools have been removed. ai.title: AgentStore: Reduce motion animation usage
ai.summary: AgentStore page replaces Framer Motion with CSS transitions in virtualized lists to improve performance. Data normalization via `select` prevents reference changes and precomputes sort fields. `getAgentsForRow` refactored to compute rows on-demand instead of pre-building `allAgentsRows`.

eli5.text: You're browsing the AgentStore page and scrolling through the long list of available agents. The page used to animate each agent card as it appeared on screen, but those animations were making scrolling feel sluggish, especially when loading many agents at once. The animations have been removed from the main list, so agent cards now appear instantly as you scroll, while the smaller Editors' Choice section still has its gentle hover effects. The page also loads slightly faster because it now calculates which agents to display only when needed, rather than preparing all of them ahead of time.

ai.title: Improve agent store list virtualization and layout
ai.summary: Refactored `web/src/app/store/page.tsx` to improve virtualization performance and mobile responsiveness. Implemented dynamic overscan calculation based on device type (mobile/touch vs desktop) and added measurement caching with debounced resize/orientation listeners. UI adjustments include enforcing consistent card minimum heights to reduce layout shifts, hiding the version badge, moving tags to a different location or removing them from the card body, and hiding the copy button on mobile viewports.

eli5.text: The agent store page now loads faster and looks more stable when scrolling through the list of agents, especially on phones and tablets. When you browse the full list, only the agents currently visible on your screen are loaded into memory, with extra rows pre-loaded around them so scrolling feels smooth - and the number of extra rows automatically increases on touch devices or smaller screens. As you resize your browser or rotate your phone, the layout recalculates cleanly without flickering or jumping cards, because each card now keeps a fixed minimum height. You also see a cleaner card layout: the small version number badge is gone, the copy-to-clipboard button hides on mobile screens, and the tags that used to sit at the bottom of each card have been removed from view.

Server-side session fetching removed from page.tsx; client handles auth via useSession. New RelativeTime component replaces formatRelativeTime to avoid hydration mismatches during SSG. Cache headers updated to max-age=600, s-maxage=600, stale-while-revalidate=600.

eli5.text: The Agent Store page now loads faster because it builds the page ahead of time and only refreshes the agent list every 10 minutes instead of every minute. If you're browsing the store, you'll see the same agents for up to 10 minutes before new ones appear, but the page will start showing your login status a moment after it loads instead of waiting on the server. The timestamp next to each agent ("2 hours ago") now updates in your browser rather than being locked in when the page was built, so it stays roughly accurate as time passes. This is live now, so you can look at the store and notice these differences today.

ai.title: Enable SSG for store page
ai.summary: Enables Static Site Generation (SSG) for the store page by adding `force-static` and `force-cache` exports in `web/src/app/store/page.tsx`. Introduces a loading skeleton component `web/src/app/store/loading.tsx` to handle static rendering states. Optimizes the agents API cache headers in `web/src/app/api/agents/route.ts` by adjusting `max-age` to 300s, increasing `stale-while-revalidate` to 3600s, and explicitly setting `Content-Type`.

eli5.text: Visitors to the store page will now see a simple loading animation with placeholder shapes while the page prepares, instead of a blank screen or delayed content. The store page has been switched to build as a static page ahead of time, which means it loads faster and can be served from a global cache, with the content refreshing automatically every ten minutes. Additionally, the agents list that the store page pulls from is now cached for a shorter duration of five minutes, while allowing cached copies to stay fresh for up to an hour, and responses are explicitly labeled with their type so browsers and caches handle them consistently.

ai.title: SDK v0.3.0 introduces new CodebuffClient interface
ai.summary: SDK v0.3.0 replaces the `CodebuffClient` implementation with a new `run` function in `sdk/src/run.ts`. `client.ts` now delegates to this new interface, removing direct WebSocket handling and tool execution logic from the client class. `custom-tool.ts` updates `CustomToolDefinition` to enforce `ToolResultOutput[]` returns and blocks reserved tool names via type constraints. The README example demonstrates the new `previousRun` chaining pattern for session continuity.

eli5.text: When you ask Codebuff to do a coding task, you now get back a result object you can save and hand back for a follow-up, instead of starting each conversation from scratch. Behind the scenes, the connection logic was moved into a single, simpler entry point, so the same agent can keep context between runs. You'll notice this if you chain two prompts together: the second one will remember what the first one created or changed without you having to paste or describe it again. This behavior is active today for anyone using the SDK.

eli5.text: When the internal evaluation system that scores how well the coding assistant performs runs its tests, it now handles error messages more gracefully. Previously, if something went wrong during a test run, the system could crash or behave unpredictably because it didn't properly capture what failed. Now, when an error occurs, the system records a description of the error and, if the test can't produce a result, it safely stops that test instead of breaking the whole evaluation. This only affects the behind-the-scenes tools used to measure the coding assistant's performance, so you wouldn't notice any difference in your own experience.

ai.title: Persist tool errors in message history
ai.summary: Tool errors now persist in message history via `toolResultsToAddAfterStream`. `run-agent-step.ts` adds explicit `Message[]` typing to `expireMessages`. `stream-parser.ts` imports `cloneDeep` to safely append `ToolMessage` objects post-stream. Internal backend refactor.

eli5.text: When the assistant tried to use a tool and that tool failed, the failure wasn't being remembered, so it could repeat the same broken step. Now, tool errors are saved alongside the conversation history, letting follow-up turns see that a tool didn't work and avoid retrying it blindly. Engineers working on the assistant's decision-making will notice the history is more complete when reviewing a session.

ai.summary: Added `backend/src/__tests__/malformed-tool-call.test.ts` covering `processStreamWithTools` edge cases. Tests verify error handling for invalid JSON, unknown tools, and mixed valid/invalid streams. Ensures tool result errors correctly populate message history and `toolResults` array.

eli5.text: The system now has a set of checks that watch how it reacts when the assistant tries to use a tool but sends something broken, like instructions written in the wrong format or a request for a tool that doesn't exist. These checks make sure that when that happens, the system records the mistake properly instead of passing bad information along or losing track of where things went wrong. You wouldn't see this directly unless you were looking at logs or testing edge cases, but it means the system handles messy or incomplete inputs more reliably instead of crashing or silently dropping parts of a conversation.
